# cyber:cyber

> Independent product design and development by Dan Andrews. Brand, interface and production code, from first direction through to release.

cyber:cyber is Dan Andrews’s independent product design and development practice in London. The work spans the whole stack of a product: brand, interface, and the code underneath — including the technical surfaces most designers hand off. Engagements are fixed-scope and fixed-price, measured in weeks rather than quarters, and deliberately few per year.

The lab's own products are the proof rather than a client list: Kaido (clinical rehab planning), Granite and Frame (native iOS apps), all designed and built in-house, plus one delivered client engagement (IKARAO, for Bittensor). The cases show product captures, generated identity output and explicitly labelled presentation studies. Kaido screens use fictional demo cases; they do not report clinical outcomes.

The site itself is hand-coded vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step and no framework — one self-contained file per page. That is a deliberate position, argued in the journal note "The hardest client was us".

## Core

- [Home](https://www.cybercyber.ai/): Independent design and development, the work, and the engagement options.
- [Manifesto](https://www.cybercyber.ai/manifesto.html): Ten things a product design lab believes — on judgement, refusal, and what's worth building rather than just shipping fast.
- [Journal](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal.html): Working notes on judgement, refusal, and building on the frontier.
- [The Register](https://www.cybercyber.ai/specimen.html): The house type specimen published as law — one variable face, seven permitted weights, eight sizes, a seeded setting machine, and the measured drift the rules haven't caught up with.

## Work

- [Kaido](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-kaido.html): Criteria-based rehab planning for physiotherapy clinics. Patients, rehabilitation plans and progress in one clinic workspace. Spun off Granite's coaching engine, piloting in clinics at £200/month.
- [Granite](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-granite.html): A native, on-device strength coach for athletes whose sport isn't lifting — rewrites your training every week around what your sport already cost your body. The engine that Kaido grew out of.
- [Frame](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-frame.html): A native BJJ training journal built against the forgetting curve.
- [IKARAO](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-ikarao.html): A generative identity system for Bittensor, art-directed off eighty-six reference textiles and enforced by a drawing engine rather than a style guide. The one client engagement among the four; the rest are the lab's own products.

## Journal

- [The sea lion papers](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-sea-lion.html): Ninety fabricated research citations, caught by checking every one against PubMed — and what a clinical product owes a clinician after that.
- [The word before it drifted](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-the-word.html): cyber comes from the Greek for helmsman, and "governor" is the same word by a different road — what that means for a studio whose products are literally feedback loops with a human at the wheel.
- [The hardest client was us](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-hardest-client.html): Why the lab's own site was treated as the hardest brief of the year — hand-built, with product captures and presentation studies clearly distinguished.
- [Nobody wrote it down](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-undocumented.html): On confabulation, contextual inquiry, and why almost no software will make a decision.
- [The velocity gods](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-velocity.html): How speed stopped being a means and became a faith — what the cult of shipping fast produces, and what it costs.
- [Building cyber:cyber](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-building.html): An honest working note on building a one-person AI product lab — how it got built and what it cost.
- [Shipping got commoditised](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-shipping.html): Anyone can ship a product in a weekend now. What's actually scarce once production is free.
- [Six things native AI features get right](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-six-things.html): The six decisions that separate native AI from a chat bubble in the corner.
- [Why cyber:cyber exists](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-why.html): The founding note — why a lab rather than an agency, and why the internet is drowning in B+ AI output.

## The offer

- The Design Block — £5,000 per week. Design shipped in a week, brand through to the technical surfaces.
- The Build — from £50,000. A complete native product taken from nothing to live.
- The Partnership — from £12,000 per month. A senior partner embedded two to three days a week.

## Who

- Dan Andrews — designer, London. A decade across brand, interface, motion and interaction, including Spotify, Epic Games and Dell, and early-stage teams before and since. Drawn to complex domains — the kind where you have to learn the subject before you can design in it. Personal site: [iamdanandrews.com](https://iamdanandrews.com).
- There is no bench and no account team; the person who designs it is the person who builds it.

## Contact

- Email: hello@cybercyber.ai — one sentence about what you're trying to ship is enough. No discovery calls.
